And $P_i P_j = \frac{1}{(x-x_i)(x-x_j)}$
So $P_i P_j (P_j - P_i) = \frac{x_j - x_i}{(x-x_i)^2(x-x_j)^2}$

# Derivative of the Rational Function

## Setting Up the Problem

I interpret the function (the natural non-trivial reading, since a literal product would cancel to a constant) as the **rational sum** form:

$$r(x) = \frac{N(x)}{D(x)}, \qquad N(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{w_i f_i}{x-x_i},\qquad D(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{w_i}{x-x_i}$$

## Applying the Quotient Rule

$$r'(x)=\frac{N'(x)\,D(x)-N(x)\,D'(x)}{[D(x)]^2}$$

Since $\dfrac{d}{dx}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{x-x_i}\right)=-\dfrac{1}{(x-x_i)^2}$, I define $P_i=\frac{1}{x-x_i}$ so that $P_i'=-P_i^{\,2}$. Then:

$$N'=-\sum_i w_i f_i\,P_i^2,\qquad D'=-\sum_i w_i\,P_i^2$$

## Expanding the Numerator

$$N'D-ND' = -\sum_{i,j}w_iw_j f_i\,P_i^2 P_j \;+\;\sum_{i,j}w_iw_j f_i\,P_i P_j^2$$

$$= \sum_{i,j} w_i w_j f_i\;P_i P_j\,(P_j-P_i)$$

Now compute the key difference:

$$P_j - P_i = \frac{1}{x-x_j}-\frac{1}{x-x_i} = \frac{x_j-x_i}{(x-x_i)(x-x_j)}$$

and therefore:

$$P_i P_j(P_j-P_i) = \frac{x_j-x_i}{(x-x_i)^2(x-x_j)^2}$$

## Assembling the Result

Since the $i=j$ terms vanish ($x_j-x_i=0$), only $i\neq j$ contributes:

$$\boxed{r'(x)=\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{\substack{j=1\\ j\neq i}}^{n}\frac{w_i\,w_j\,f_i\,(x_j-x_i)}{(x-x_i)^2\,(x-x_j)^2}}{\displaystyle\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n}\frac{w_j}{x-x_j}\right)^2}}$$

Equivalently, pairing each unordered pair $\{i,j\}$ once:

$$r'(x)=\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}\frac{w_i\,w_j\,(f_i-f_j)\,(x_j-x_i)}{(x-x_i)^2\,(x-x_j)^2}}{\displaystyle\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n}\frac{w_j}{x-x_j}\right)^2}$$

### Quick verification ($n=2$)

For $n=2$, the numerator reduces to $\dfrac{w_1 w_2(f_1-f_2)(x_2-x_1)}{(x-x_1)^2(x-x_2)^2}$, and the denominator becomes $\left(\dfrac{w_1}{x-x_1}+\dfrac{w_2}{x-x_2}\right)^2$. This matches the derivative of the Möbius form $\dfrac{ax+b}{cx+d}$: $\;r'=\dfrac{w_1 w_2(f_1-f_2)(x_2-x_1)}{\bigl[w_1(x-x_2)+w_2(x-x_1)\bigr]^2}$. ✓
